title: Listing
description: One listing: a plug-in or a piece of content. This is the file a pull request adds as sources/<publisher>/<uid>/listing.json. Paths are relative to that directory. A sha256 given on an asset is checked against the file it names; the build fills in any that are left out. The signed listing.json a client reads is the same document with every asset path rewritten to its target, every sha256 filled in, and each version's definition and example moved into its manifest target (entry.schema.json).

listing_base.description: What a source listing and a published entry share. Each narrows 'versions' to its own shape.

uid.description: The catalogue code: 14 characters of Crockford base32 without I, L, O or U. Assigned by the publisher, never reused.

public_id.description: '<publisher>.<slug>'. The part before the first dot must equal publisher.

publisher.description: The publisher's prefix. Must have a record under publishers/.

kind.description: What is listed: a plug-in ('plugin'), an automation ('auto'), a pack of profile decorations ('profile_pack'), or one tool's content, named by the tool.

summary.description: One or two sentences shown on the listing's card.

description.description: The longer text on the listing's page. Markdown.

price.description: Null for a free listing. The public target refuses any listing whose price is not null.

plugin_api_version.description: A plug-in API contract version, 'MAJOR.MINOR': the plug-in SDK release whose published spec a plug-in was built against.

path.description: A relative path inside the listing's directory.

version_base.description: What every version gives, as a source and as published.

min_app_version.description: The oldest Initiative release this version runs on.

min_plugin_api.description: The oldest plug-in API contract this version needs, as the kit manifest's min_plugin_api gives it. Absent, the version runs on any contract.

document.description: A JSON object: a path to a JSON file inside the listing's directory, or the object inline.

source_version.description: One version as the source gives it. The build publishes it as the target <version>/manifest.json: {uid, public_id, kind, definition, example?}.

definition.description: What installs. For a plug-in, its kit manifest: a container's names the listing's public_id as its service.public_id, and a declarative plug-in's has no service block. For a tool's content, that tool's definition.

example.description: Optional, for a tool's content only: the filled-in example shown beside the listing.

registration.description: For a plug-in (and allowed for an automation): what kind it is, the most it may ever be granted, and the reference sectors it may learn. A container names the image each deployment runs, and each deployment gives its location and the keys its copy signs with. A declarative plug-in names no image: Initiative runs it from its manifest.

image.description: A container's image, pinned by digest.

scope_ceiling.description: The scopes review cleared, and 'plugins:<public_id>' for each plug-in it may call. A manifest may ask for less, never more.

reference_sectors.description: Reference sectors the plug-in may be granted. The public target refuses any listing that names one.

compose.description: For a container: its Docker Compose service, as its publisher writes it, for an operator to add beside Initiative's own.

service.description: A Docker Compose fragment, YAML text. Initiative fills two placeholders when it shows it: '${IMAGE}', the registration's image, and '${INITIATIVE_URL}', the deployment's public address. Any other '${' is refused.

base_url.description: Where the service answers on the Compose network, such as 'http://tracker:8080'. Initiative pre-fills the deployment's base URL with it.
